title: Clone Graph
description:
You are given a reference to one node of a **connected, undirected graph**. Each node has an integer `val` and a list of `neighbors`.

Return a **deep copy** (clone) of the whole graph: every node must be a brand-new object, and the copy must have exactly the same structure.

In the test data a graph is written as an adjacency list: the node with `val = i` is at index `i - 1` and the list holds the `val`s of its neighbors. An empty list means `null`.

examples.explanation: Four nodes arranged in a square. Node 1 neighbors nodes 2 and 4, and so on.
A single node with no neighbors.
An empty graph (the node is null).

constraints: 1 <= Node.val <= 100, and every val is unique
There are no repeated edges and no self-loops.
hints: Use a map from original node to its clone so each node is copied once.
Copy a node, then recursively (or with a queue) copy its neighbors and wire up the clones.
